name: platform_profile_victus_s_set_ec
prose: Precondition: profile is a platform_profile_option value; the global active_thermal_profile_params is read once at entry and is either NULL or points to a valid thermal_profile_params. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV if active_thermal_profile_params is NULL, and returns -EOPNOTSUPP if profile is not PLATFORM_PROFILE_PERFORMANCE, PLATFORM_PROFILE_BALANCED or PLATFORM_PROFILE_LOW_POWER; both of these returns happen before any WMI query is issued. Otherwise it calls hp_wmi_get_fan_count_userdefine_trigger() and ignores its result, then calls omen_thermal_profile_set() with the profile's thermal value (params->performance, balanced or low_power) and returns that call's result if it is negative (logging with pr_err), then calls victus_s_gpu_thermal_profile_set() with the per-profile GPU flags (ctgp, ppab, dstate = 1) and returns its result if it is negative (the CPU thermal profile has then already been set and is not rolled back), and returns 0 when both calls returned non-negative values (a positive value from either call is not propagated). The function acquires no lock and takes no reference or memory.
note: reviewer (formal contract only bounds the return value) right; contract removed because the function reads a global and issues WMI queries (hp-wmi.c:1733-1784).

name: pmc_core_get_tgl_lpm_reqs
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device whose driver data is an initialized pmc_dev with a valid pmcs[PMC_IDX_MAIN] entry whose map is valid. Postcondition: returns nothing. If the device has no ACPI companion it returns immediately with no ACPI call. Otherwise it evaluates _DSM function ACPI_GET_LOW_MODE_REGISTERS typed as a buffer; if the evaluation returns NULL (including a wrong result type) it logs a debug message, and if the returned buffer length differs from lpm_size (LPM_MAX_NUM_MODES * lpm_num_maps * 4) it logs a different debug message; in both of those cases pmc->lpm_req_regs is left unchanged. If the length matches it calls devm_kcalloc for lpm_size elements of sizeof(u32) (that is, lpm_size * 4 bytes, zeroed); if that allocation fails the function skips the copy and logs no message; otherwise it copies lpm_size bytes from the _DSM buffer into the start of the new allocation and stores the allocation in pmc->lpm_req_regs. On every path after the _DSM call the object is passed to ACPI_FREE (a NULL object when the evaluation failed).
note: reviewer (allocation is lpm_size * sizeof(u32) bytes, not lpm_size bytes) right, tgl.c:276-277 and memcpy of lpm_size bytes at 281. Slice starts mid-function; read from tgl.c:240.

name: intel_pmt_get_regions_by_feature
prose: Precondition: id is a pmt_feature_id value. Postcondition: if pmt_feature_id_is_valid(id) is false it returns ERR_PTR(-EINVAL). Otherwise it holds ep_lock (released automatically at return) while it counts the entries in telem_array whose feature_flags have BIT(id) set; if the count is zero it returns ERR_PTR(-ENOENT); if kzalloc of the pmt_feature_group with count regions fails it returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM). It then walks telem_array again and, for each entry with BIT(id) set, fills the next region from the entry through pmt_copy_region; if pmt_copy_region returns an error it returns ERR_PTR of that error and the partly filled group is freed with kfree through the __free cleanup. On success it initializes the group's kref to 1 and returns the group (ownership passes to the caller, who releases it with intel_pmt_put_feature_group); the group's count field is set to the first-pass count.
note: listed name pmt_telem_get_regions_by_feature does not exist; the function in the slice is intel_pmt_get_regions_by_feature (telemetry.c:245-290), slice cut its tail. Fixed under the real name. Both passes over telem_array run under ep_lock.

name: sdsi_status_to_errno
prose: Precondition: none; status is any u32. Postcondition: returns 0 when status equals SDSI_MBOX_CMD_SUCCESS (0x40), -ETIMEDOUT (-110) when status equals SDSI_MBOX_CMD_TIMEOUT (0x80), and -EIO (-5) for every other value of status. It reads and writes no state and takes no locks.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (status == 0x40 && result == 0) || (status == 0x80 && result == -110) || (status != 0x40 && status != 0x80 && result == -5); */
note: sdsi.c:150-160; old contract had a spurious requires and omitted nothing real, rewritten as a plain disjunction.

name: save_settings_store
prose: Precondition: buf is the sysfs input string and count its length; the caller does not hold tlmi_mutex. Postcondition: it first calls sysfs_match_string on save_mode_strings; if that returns a negative value it is returned immediately, before tlmi_mutex is taken and with no state changed. Otherwise it takes tlmi_mutex and releases it on every later return, and frees the temporary auth string (if any) on every later return. For the modes "single" and "bulk" it sets tlmi_priv.save_mode to the matching index and returns count. For "save" it returns -EOPNOTSUPP if can_set_bios_settings is false or save_mode is TLMI_SAVE_SINGLE, then -ENOENT if save_required is false, then, if certificate_support is set and pwd_admin->cert_installed, -EINVAL if the admin signature or save_signature is NULL, otherwise it calls tlmi_simple_call with the save signature and returns its error without changing save_required or reboot_required if it fails. If instead opcode_support is set, when pwd_enabled and a non-empty password exist it calls tlmi_opcode_setting for the admin password and returns its error early (state unchanged) if that fails, then calls tlmi_save_bios_settings(""); if neither certificate nor opcode path applies (legacy), it builds an auth string with kasprintf when pwd_enabled and a password exist (returning -ENOMEM on failure) and calls tlmi_save_bios_settings with it, or with "" when no password applies. In the opcode and legacy cases, and in the certificate case when the call succeeded, save_required is set false and reboot_required is set true regardless of the save result; then, if the save result is 0 and pending_changes was false, pending_changes becomes true and a KOBJ_CHANGE uevent is sent on the class device. The function returns the save result if it is non-zero, otherwise count.
note: reviewer (round 15: mutex is not acquired when sysfs_match_string fails) right; earlier prose said the mutex was taken in every case. save_settings_store at think-lmi.c:1301-1382.

name: hotkey_get_wlsw
prose: Precondition: none; it may be called whenever tpacpi data is initialized. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV (-19) if tp_features.hotkey_wlsw is not set. Otherwise, when CONFIG_THINKPAD_ACPI_DEBUGFACILITIES is built in and dbg_wlswemul is set, it returns TPACPI_RFK_RADIO_ON (1) if tpacpi_wlsw_emulstate is non-zero and TPACPI_RFK_RADIO_OFF (0) otherwise without evaluating ACPI. In the normal case it evaluates the WLSW method on hkey_handle with acpi_evalf; if that fails it returns -EIO (-5); otherwise it returns TPACPI_RFK_RADIO_ON (1) if the returned status is non-zero and TPACPI_RFK_RADIO_OFF (0) if it is zero. It takes no lock and modifies no state.
note: thinkpad_acpi.c:1951-1968. Contract removed: function reads globals (tp_features, hkey_handle, debug emulation state).

name: kbdlight_get_level
prose: Precondition: none beyond driver initialization (hkey_handle is a global that may be NULL). Postcondition: returns -ENXIO (-6) if hkey_handle is NULL; otherwise it evaluates the MLCG method with argument 0 and returns -EIO (-5) if that evaluation fails; if it succeeds and the reported status is negative it returns that status unchanged; if the status is non-negative it returns status & 0x3 (a value in 0..3). It takes no locks and holds no references.
note: reviewer (formal contract allows any negative result, weaker than the code) right; contract dropped because the function reads the global hkey_handle. thinkpad_acpi.c:5065-5079.

name: volume_alsa_set_volume
prose: Precondition: vol is the requested level (u8, 0..255). Postcondition: the function logs a debug message and returns the value of __volume_set_volume_ec(vol): -EINVAL if vol exceeds TP_EC_VOLUME_MAX (14), before taking any lock; otherwise it takes volume_mutex with mutex_lock_killable and returns -EINTR if that is interrupted; otherwise it reads the EC audio status and returns -EIO if the read fails. It computes the new status as the old status with its low four bits (TP_EC_AUDIO_LVL_MSK) replaced by vol; if the new status equals the old status it returns 0 without writing; otherwise it writes the new status to the EC (which sleeps 1 ms after a successful write) and returns -EIO if the write fails or 1 if it succeeds. volume_mutex is released on every path after it was taken.
note: volume_alsa_set_volume is a wrapper at thinkpad_acpi.c:7298-7303; behaviour from __volume_set_volume_ec (7219-7245), volume_get_status_ec, volume_set_status_ec. Contract removed (global mutex, EC access).

name: msi_wmi_notify
prose: Precondition: obj is the ACPI object delivered by the WMI core (it may be NULL); msi_wmi_input_dev and event_wmi are set up by module init. Postcondition: returns nothing. If obj is NULL or not an ACPI_TYPE_INTEGER it only logs 'Unknown event received'. Otherwise it uses the integer as scancode and looks it up in the sparse keymap; if no entry exists it logs 'Unknown key pressed' and returns. If event_wmi->quirk_last_pressed is set and less than 50 ms have passed since last_pressed it logs a debug 'Suppressed' message and returns without updating last_pressed; if the quirk is set and 50 ms or more have passed, last_pressed is set to the current real time. Then, if the entry type is KE_KEY and either the global backlight device pointer is non-NULL or the scancode is neither MSI_KEY_BRIGHTNESSUP nor MSI_KEY_BRIGHTNESSDOWN, it logs a debug 'Send key' message and calls sparse_keymap_report_entry with value 1 and autorelease true. Entries of other types (for example KE_IGNORE), and brightness keys while backlight is NULL, are not reported and no message is logged for them.
note: reviewer (round 15: brightness keys are reported when backlight is registered, dropped when it is not) right; the old prose had it reversed and called the last argument autorepeat (it is the autorelease parameter). msi-wmi.c:173-213.

name: acpi_pcc_hotkey_add
prose: Precondition: device is an ACPI device pointer. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if device is NULL; returns -ENODEV (logging) if the SQTY count is not greater than SINF_DC_CUR_BRIGHT or is greater than 255, with nothing allocated; returns -ENOMEM if kzalloc of the pcc structure fails (nothing allocated) or if kcalloc of pcc->sinf fails (the pcc is freed; device->driver_data has not been set yet). After those, device->driver_data is set to pcc and the ACPI device name and class strings are set. The later steps, in order, and what a failure there undoes: acpi_pcc_init_input failing returns its error after freeing sinf and pcc (the input device is not unregistered here); failure to retrieve BIOS data returns -EIO after unregistering the input device and freeing sinf and pcc; when acpi_video_get_backlight_type() is acpi_backlight_vendor, a backlight_device_register failure returns its error after the input-device unregister and frees; sysfs_create_group failure returns its error after unregistering the backlight device, the input device and freeing; if check_optd_present succeeds, platform_device_register_simple failure returns its error after removing the sysfs group, unregistering the backlight and input device and freeing, and device_create_file failure returns its error after additionally unregistering the platform device. On every one of these failure paths from init_input onward device->driver_data is left pointing at the freed pcc. On success it has reset the sticky-key mode to 0, cached brightness/mute/eco values from sinf, registered the i8042 filter (its return is ignored) and returns 0 with the input device, sysfs group, optional backlight and optional platform device left registered.
note: reviewer (round 15: early allocation failures do not free anything or leave driver_data dangling) right. Slice cut the head; function at panasonic-laptop.c:994-1121.

name: pmc_atom_init
prose: Precondition: runs once at device_initcall time in process context (__init). Postcondition: it iterates all PCI devices with for_each_pci_dev and, for the first one for which pci_match_id(pmc_pci_ids, pdev) matches, returns pmc_setup_dev(pdev, ent) at once (the loop's reference on that pci_dev is not dropped before returning); if no device matches it returns -ENODEV. pmc_setup_dev returns -ENOMEM if ioremap of the PMC registers fails (after it has already read the ACPI base address, possibly installed pm_power_off, and read pmc_device.base_addr, and without setting pmc_device.init); otherwise it sets up registers, debugfs and s2idle registration, sets pmc_device.init to true, and returns 0, or the non-zero error from pmc_setup_clks (-ENOMEM or the PTR_ERR of platform_device_register_data) which is only logged with a warning, after those other effects have happened. Global state touched on paths that reach pmc_setup_dev: acpi_base_addr, pm_power_off (when acpi_base_addr is non-zero and pm_power_off was NULL), pmc_device fields, the ioremap mapping, debugfs entries and the s2idle registration.
note: reviewer (formal contract weaker than prose) right; contract dropped (global state). pmc_atom.c:578-599 and pmc_setup_dev 529-569.

name: sony_nc_thermal_mode_get
prose: Precondition: the SNC interface is initialized (sony_call_snc_handle uses driver globals). Postcondition: calls sony_call_snc_handle(0x0122, 0x0100, &result); if that returns non-zero (including an error from locating the handle) it returns -EIO (-5); otherwise it returns result & 0xff (a value in 0..255). The function itself writes no driver variables and takes no lock.
note: sony-laptop.c:2162-2170; contract removed because the callee uses global ACPI state.

name: uv_hubs_init
prose: Precondition: uv_bios_obj_cnt holds the BIOS hub count, sgi_uv_kobj is a registered kobject and uv_master_nasid is set. Postcondition: it allocates prev_obj_to_cnode (kmalloc_array; -ENOMEM on failure with nothing else done) and sets each entry to INVALID_CNODE, creates the kset "hubs" (-ENOMEM on failure, then frees prev_obj_to_cnode), allocates hub_buf (-ENOMEM on failure, then unregisters the kset and frees prev_obj_to_cnode), fills it with uv_bios_enum_objs (a non-zero return gives -EINVAL, after freeing hub_buf, unregistering the kset and freeing prev_obj_to_cnode), allocates uv_hubs (-ENOMEM, same cleanup), then for each hub allocates the entry (-ENOMEM on failure), points it at hub_buf[i], caches its cnode, sets the kset and calls kobject_init_and_add; if that returns an error the function returns that errno as is (not necessarily -ENOMEM or -EINVAL). On a failure inside the hub loop it puts the kobjects of the hubs already initialised (including the one whose kobject_init_and_add failed, but not one whose allocation failed), frees the uv_hubs array, then frees hub_buf, unregisters the kset and frees prev_obj_to_cnode; the global pointers are not reset to NULL. On success it sends a KOBJ_ADD uevent for each hub and returns 0, leaving uv_hubs, hub_buf, uv_hubs_kset and prev_obj_to_cnode allocated as globals.
note: reviewer (kobject_init_and_add errno is returned unchanged, may differ from -ENOMEM/-EINVAL) right. Slice cut the head; function at uv_sysfs.c:213-284.

name: imx8m_blk_ctrl_power_on
prose: Precondition: genpd is the genpd member of an imx8m_blk_ctrl_domain set up by probe (valid data, clks, paths, power_dev and bc). Postcondition: it holds bc->power_lock from entry until it returns, on every return path. It first calls pm_runtime_get_sync on bc->bus_power_dev; if that is negative it calls pm_runtime_put_noidle on the bus device, logs, and returns that error, touching nothing else. Otherwise it clears the BLK_SFT_RSTN bits (and BLK_MIPI_RESET_DIV bits if mipi_phy_rst_mask is non-zero), then calls clk_bulk_prepare_enable on the domain clocks; if that fails it returns the error after pm_runtime_put on the bus device (clk_bulk_prepare_enable itself undoes partial enables; the reset bits stay cleared). It then sets (or, for is_errata_err050531, clears) the BLK_CLK_EN bits and calls pm_runtime_get_sync on domain->power_dev; if that is negative it disables/unprepares the clocks, calls pm_runtime_put on the bus device and returns the error without any put on domain->power_dev, so the usage count taken by the failed get_sync is not dropped by this function. On success it sets BLK_CLK_EN (errata case), waits 5 us, sets the reset bits again, calls icc_bulk_set_bw (a failure is only logged), disables/unprepares the clocks and returns 0, leaving the runtime-PM references on both bc->bus_power_dev and domain->power_dev held. Return values of the regmap bit operations are ignored.
note: reviewer round 15 (domain->power_dev get_sync failure is not followed by put_noidle) right; round 2 (clk failure skips clock disable) was consistent with the prose and the code (clk_bulk_prepare_enable cleans up itself), wrong. imx8m-blk-ctrl.c:101-168.

name: imx8m_blk_ctrl_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device whose OF match data points to a valid imx8m_blk_ctrl_data (the match data is used without a NULL check). Postcondition: returns -ENOMEM if the bc structure, bc->domains or onecell_data.domains devm allocation fails; returns the devm_mutex_init error, PTR_ERR of the ioremap result, or the regmap init error (via dev_err_probe), each before any power-domain attach. It then attaches the "bus" power domain; on an error it returns -EPROBE_DEFER if the error is -ENODEV and the error itself otherwise. In the per-domain loop it fills clock and interconnect-path descriptors, calls devm_of_icc_bulk_get (an error other than -EPROBE_DEFER only produces a warning and sets that domain's num_paths to 0; -EPROBE_DEFER aborts), devm_clk_bulk_get, dev_pm_domain_attach_by_name for the GPC domain (-ENODEV if it returns NULL, else PTR_ERR) and pm_genpd_init (after which a failure detaches that domain's power device), storing each genpd in the onecell array. After the loop it calls of_genpd_add_provider_onecell, dev_pm_genpd_add_notifier on the bus power device, dev_set_drvdata and devm_of_platform_populate, returning 0 only if all of those succeed. On any failure from the loop or after it, the already registered genpds are removed with pm_genpd_remove and their power devices detached, the bus power device is detached, and if the provider had been added of_genpd_del_provider is called first (the power notifier added before devm_of_platform_populate is not removed by the cleanup labels); the error code of the failing call is returned.
note: reviewer (round 15: success does not require interconnect paths; non-defer ICC failure is ignored) right. Slice cut the head; function at imx8m-blk-ctrl.c:196-365.

name: imx93_blk_ctrl_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device whose OF match data points to a valid imx93_blk_ctrl_data (it is dereferenced for the regmap config without a NULL check), with consistent num_domains, num_clks, domains, clk_names and skip_mask. Postcondition: returns 0 after devm allocation of bc, ioremap and regmap init, devm allocation of bc->domains and onecell_data.domains, getting the bus clocks, then for each domain not in skip_mask getting its clocks, initialising its genpd with pm_genpd_init and registering a devm release action, and storing it in the onecell array (skipped domains keep a NULL entry); then for each non-skipped domain with a parent other than BLK_CTRL_NO_PARENT allocating a link, calling pm_genpd_add_subdomain and registering a devm release action; then devm_pm_runtime_enable, of_genpd_add_provider_onecell and a devm action that deletes the provider. It returns a negative errno on the first failure: -ENOMEM from the devm allocations (no log), the ioremap error, the regmap init error, or the error from devm_clk_bulk_get (bus or domain clocks), pm_genpd_init, devm_add_action_or_reset, pm_genpd_add_subdomain, devm_pm_runtime_enable or of_genpd_add_provider_onecell. Resources registered through devm or devm actions are released by the driver core on failure, so the function frees nothing itself.
note: reviewer (error list omits pm_genpd_add_subdomain failure) right. Real name imx93_blk_ctrl_probe (imx93-blk-ctrl.c:222-362); slice cut the head.

name: brcmstb_reboot_probe_helper_unused
note: no such function in brcmstb-reboot.c (functions are brcmstb_restart_handler, brcmstb_reboot_probe, brcmstb_reboot_init, lines 32-121).

name: ab8500_chargalg_algorithm
prose: Precondition: di is a valid ab8500_chargalg whose bm->bi battery info and work queue are initialised. Postcondition: returns nothing. It collects data from all power supplies (power_supply_for_each_psy), then calls ab8500_chargalg_end_of_charge, _check_temp, _check_charger_voltage and _check_charger_connection; on an AB8500 it also calls _check_charger_enable and only logs a negative result. It then picks at most one event-driven transition with an if/else-if chain in this order: no charger connected, or unknown battery when chg_unknown_bat is not allowed, moves to STATE_HANDHELD_INIT unless already in STATE_HANDHELD (also clearing safety_timer_expired); safety timer expired, battery removed, main/USB charger not ok (not when vbus_collapsed is set), overvoltage or charger-not-ok, hardware thermal protection, battery temperature under/over, watchdog expired, and battery temperature low/high each move to their *_INIT state unless already in the corresponding state. It logs a debug status line and then runs a switch on the (possibly just changed) charge_state: the HANDHELD, BATT_REMOVED, HW_TEMP_PROTECT, OVV_PROTECT, CHG_NOT_OK, SAFETY_TIMER_EXPIRED, WD_EXPIRED and TEMP_UNDEROVER *_INIT states stop charging, advance to the matching steady state and fall through to it (HANDHELD_INIT also sets the charge status to discharging); NORMAL_INIT stops charging if the battery's constant charge current limit is 0 and otherwise starts charging with the battery-info limits, then moves to NORMAL, restarts the safety timer, stops the maintenance timer and sets the status to charging; WAIT_FOR_RECHARGE_INIT holds charging; MAINTENANCE_A/B_INIT and TEMP_LOWHIGH_INIT start charging with the maintenance-table or alert-temperature limits; the steady protection states (BATT_REMOVED, HW_TEMP_PROTECT, OVV_PROTECT, CHG_NOT_OK, WD_EXPIRED, TEMP_UNDEROVER, TEMP_LOWHIGH) return to STATE_NORMAL_INIT once their triggering events are gone; HANDHELD and SAFETY_TIMER_EXPIRED stay as they are; NORMAL handles the Maxim current ramp and moves to WAIT_FOR_RECHARGE_INIT or MAINTENANCE_A_INIT when the battery is full and maintenance charging is active; WAIT_FOR_RECHARGE, MAINTENANCE_A and MAINTENANCE_B return to NORMAL_INIT when ab8500_chargalg_time_to_restart is true or, for the maintenance states, move on or back when the maintenance timer has expired; MAINTENANCE_A_INIT and MAINTENANCE_B_INIT return to NORMAL_INIT if the battery info has no matching maintenance setting; TEMP_LOWHIGH_INIT with neither temperature event set logs an error and returns to NORMAL_INIT. After the switch, if charge_state is STATE_NORMAL_INIT, MAINTENANCE_A_INIT or MAINTENANCE_B_INIT it queues chargalg_work on chargalg_wq.
note: previously dropped as 'enclosing function not shown'; the function exists (ab8500_chargalg.c:1225-1580), slice shows only the switch. Read in full. Summary prose rather than per-state enumeration; no claim of exhaustive state coverage.

name: ab8500_charger_ac_en
prose: Precondition: charger is a ux500_charger embedded in the AC part of an ab8500_charger. Postcondition: when enable is non-zero: if di->ac.charger_connected is false it returns -ENXIO immediately. Otherwise, if vddadc_en_ac is false it calls regulator_enable; a failure is only logged and leaves vddadc_en_ac false, success sets it true and the regulator then stays enabled on every later return. It then converts vset_uv, iset_ua and ac_curr_max_ua to register values and returns -ENXIO if any of them is negative. It then writes the voltage-level register, sets the main input current and the output current, and writes MCH_CTRL1 (MAIN_CH_ENA, with the no-overshoot bit when bm->enable_overshoot is false), returning the error of the first one that fails and doing nothing after it. If all succeed it calls ab8500_charger_led_en(di, true) (a negative result is logged), sets di->ac.charger_online to 1, calls ab8500_power_supply_changed on the AC psy and returns the result of the LED call. When enable is zero: on AB8500 1.1 or earlier it queues kick_wd_work if di->ac_conn is set, writes the lowest voltage CH_VOL_LVL_3P5 and sets the output current to 0; otherwise it writes 0 to MCH_CTRL1; the first failing write is returned immediately (before the steps below). It then calls ab8500_charger_led_en(di, false) (negative result logged), sets charger_online to 0 and wd_expired to false, disables the regulator and clears vddadc_en_ac if it was set, calls ab8500_power_supply_changed on the AC psy and returns the LED call's result. The early error returns skip ab8500_power_supply_changed. It holds no lock and no reference is transferred to the caller.
note: reviewer (round 15: the AC-connected and range checks are handled by -ENXIO returns, not preconditions) right; earlier claim that regulator_enable failure is ignored is also reflected. ab8500_charger.c:1405-1570.

name: ab8500_enable_disable_sw_fallback
prose: Precondition: di is an initialised ab8500_charger. Postcondition: returns nothing. It selects the register (for AB8500: bank 0x15, reg 0x0, bit 3; otherwise AB8500_SYS_CTRL1_BLOCK, AB8500_SW_CONTROL_FALLBACK, bit 0) and reads it; if that read fails it logs and returns with no register written. On an AB8500 it then writes 0x2 to bank 0x11 reg 0x00; if that write fails it logs and skips the fallback write. Otherwise it sets the fallback bit in the value that was read if fallback is true, clears it if false, and writes the whole value back; a failure of that write is only logged. On an AB8500 it finally writes 0x0 to bank 0x11 reg 0x00, including after a failed OTP-enable write, and only logs a failure. Nothing is returned and no lock is taken; the function does not claim what the register holds after a failed write.
note: reviewer (round 15: prose claimed a failed write-back leaves the register unchanged; code only logs) right. ab8500_charger.c:350-406; slice starts before the function at 302.

name: gpio_charger_set_property
prose: Precondition: psy is a power_supply whose driver data is a struct gpio_charger and, when psp is POWER_SUPPLY_PROP_CONSTANT_CHARGE_CURRENT_MAX, val is readable and gpio_charger->current_limit_gpios is non-NULL (set_charge_current_limit reads current_limit_gpios->ndescs before testing the map size). Postcondition: for any other property it returns -EINVAL and does not read val. For POWER_SUPPLY_PROP_CONSTANT_CHARGE_CURRENT_MAX it returns the result of set_charge_current_limit(gpio_charger, val->intval): -EINVAL if current_limit_map_size is 0; otherwise it scans the map in array order for the first entry whose limit_ua (u32) is <= val->intval converted to unsigned (the map is required to be sorted descending only by probe, not here; a negative intval converts to a large unsigned value and so selects entry 0), uses the last entry if none qualifies, drives the GPIOs current_limit_gpios->desc[ndescs-1-i] to bit i of that entry's gpiodata with gpiod_set_value_cansleep, stores the entry's limit_ua in charge_current_limit, logs a debug message and returns 0.
note: round 1 (current_limit_gpios dereferenced before map-size test) right; round 2 (no dereference when no GPIOs) wrong, gpio-charger.c:59-60; round 15 (negative intval compared as unsigned) right, gpio-charger.c:67. Final claim counted as right.

name: twl4030_charger_update_current
prose: Precondition: bci is an initialised twl4030_bci whose channel_vac, ac_cur, usb_cur, usb_cur_target, ichg_eoc, ichg_lo, ichg_hi and current_worker are valid and whose TWL4030 registers are reachable over I2C. Postcondition: it first chooses the current: if ac_available(channel_vac) it uses ac_cur and sets ac_is_active true; otherwise it uses usb_cur, sets ac_is_active false, lowers usb_cur and the used value to usb_cur_target if usb_cur is above it, and schedules current_worker with USB_CUR_DELAY if the used value is below usb_cur_target. It then returns the negative status of the first failing checked I2C operation and stops there: the BCICTL1 read, the BCIMFTH8, BCIMFTH9, BCIIREF1 and BCIIREF2 reads, the BCIMFKEY key writes (before the BCIMFTH8, BCIMFTH9 and two BCIIREF writes), and the BCIIREF2 write. The PM master BOOT_BCI read, the BCIMFTH8, BCIMFTH9, BCIIREF1 and BCICTL1 writes, and twl4030_clear_set_boot_bci are not checked, so those can fail silently and the function still returns 0. When the CGAIN setting must change, twl4030_clear_set_boot_bci(boot_bci, 0) is called before the register updates and twl4030_clear_set_boot_bci(0, boot_bci) at the end after flipping CGAIN; an early error return in between skips that final step. It returns 0 if no checked operation failed.
note: reviewer (round 15: usb_cur clamp and current_worker scheduling are worker logic, not this function) wrong: twl4030_charger.c:253-265. Earlier-round point (unchecked writes) right and reflected. Function at 240-397.

name: psp_val_to_charge_mode
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns CHARGE_MODE_AC (3) for POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_TRICKLE (2), CHARGE_MODE_EXP (2) for POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_FAST (3), CHARGE_MODE_STD (1) for POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_STANDARD (4), CHARGE_MODE_AUTO (4) for POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_ADAPTIVE (5), CHARGE_MODE_CUSTOM (5) for POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_CUSTOM (6), CHARGE_MODE_LONGLIFE (6) for POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_LONGLIFE (7), and -EINVAL (-22) for every other value of psp_val. It reads and writes no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (psp_val == 2 && result == 3) || (psp_val == 3 && result == 2) || (psp_val == 4 && result == 1) || (psp_val == 5 && result == 4) || (psp_val == 6 && result == 5) || (psp_val == 7 && result == 6) || ((psp_val < 2 || psp_val > 7) && result == -22); */
note: wilco-charger.c:39-57. Old prose and contract used the wrong enum numbers (TRICKLE=1 etc.); power_supply.h:46-53 gives UNKNOWN=0, NONE=1, TRICKLE=2, FAST=3, STANDARD=4, ADAPTIVE=5, CUSTOM=6, LONGLIFE=7.

name: charge_mode_to_psp_val
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_STANDARD (4) for CHARGE_MODE_STD (1), POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_FAST (3) for CHARGE_MODE_EXP (2), POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_TRICKLE (2) for CHARGE_MODE_AC (3), POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_ADAPTIVE (5) for CHARGE_MODE_AUTO (4), POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_CUSTOM (6) for CHARGE_MODE_CUSTOM (5), POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE_LONGLIFE (7) for CHARGE_MODE_LONGLIFE (6), and -EINVAL (-22) for every other value of mode. It reads and writes no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (mode == 1 && result == 4) || (mode == 2 && result == 3) || (mode == 3 && result == 2) || (mode == 4 && result == 5) || (mode == 5 && result == 6) || (mode == 6 && result == 7) || ((mode < 1 || mode > 6) && result == -22); */
note: wilco-charger.c:60-78; old prose and contract used the wrong POWER_SUPPLY_CHARGE_TYPE numbers (see psp_val_to_charge_mode).

name: RAPL_EVENT_GROUP(_name, domain)
prose: Macro-generated function: RAPL_EVENT_GROUP(_name, domain) defines, besides an attribute array and an attribute_group, a function is_visible_<_name>(kobj, attr, event) that returns attr->mode if the global rapl_pmu.domain_map has the BIT(domain) bit set and returns 0 otherwise; it ignores kobj and event and modifies no state. The file instantiates it as is_visible_cores (RAPL_DOMAIN_PP0), is_visible_pkg (RAPL_DOMAIN_PACKAGE), is_visible_ram (RAPL_DOMAIN_DRAM), is_visible_gpu (RAPL_DOMAIN_PP1) and is_visible_psys (RAPL_DOMAIN_PLATFORM).
note: macro defined at intel_rapl_common.c:1962-1976, instantiated at 1979-1983. Name set to the macro definition head per rule 5.

name: berlin_pwm_apply
prose: Precondition: chip and pwm identify a valid Berlin PWM channel and state is the requested state; when state->enabled is true, state->period must be non-zero because berlin_pwm_config divides by it. Postcondition: let enabled be the software flag pwm->state.enabled on entry. If state->polarity differs from pwm->state.polarity, it first disables the channel when enabled was true (and treats it as disabled from then on), then writes the new polarity (berlin_pwm_set_polarity always returns 0). If state->enabled is false it then disables the channel if the local enabled flag is still true and returns 0. Otherwise it calls berlin_pwm_config: if the period needs more than the maximum count even after the 4096 prescale, that call returns -ERANGE before writing any register and apply returns -ERANGE, with any polarity change and the disable that preceded it already done (so the channel is disabled only if it was disabled by the polarity branch or was disabled before; a channel that was enabled with unchanged polarity keeps running with its previous settings); otherwise config writes the prescale, duty and period registers, and apply enables the channel (berlin_pwm_enable returns 0) if the local enabled flag is false, and returns 0.
note: reviewer (round 15: -ERANGE with unchanged polarity on an already-disabled channel leaves it disabled, not running) right: the old 'otherwise still running' wording covered that case wrongly. pwm-berlin.c:155-186, 75-111.

name: norm_to_sys_addr
prose: Precondition: df_cfg is the file's global data-fabric configuration (its rev may be UNKNOWN); socket_id, die_id, coh_st_inst_id and addr are passed by value. Postcondition: the function returns (unsigned long)-EINVAL if df_cfg.rev is UNKNOWN; it then zeroes a local addr_ctx, sets ret_addr and the inputs, and evaluates legacy_hole_en on that context before any address map has been loaded, so that test reads zero map registers and the legacy-hole -EINVAL return (taken when the test is true and df_cfg.dram_hole_base is zero) is not reachable in this function as written. It then returns (unsigned long)-EINVAL if determine_node_id, get_address_map, denormalize_address or dehash_address returns non-zero, or if addr_over_limit finds ret_addr above the DRAM limit address; between those calls it applies add_base_and_hole either before or after dehash_address depending on late_hole_remove. Otherwise it returns ctx.ret_addr, the translated system physical address. This function itself takes no lock and returns no allocation to the caller.
note: reviewer round 2 (legacy_hole_en is checked on zeroed ctx so it cannot trigger) right; round 15 (omits -EINVAL for legacy hole enabled with zero hole base) wrong, since that return needs legacy_hole_en true on a context memset to 0 (core.c:117-129, legacy_hole_en reads ctx->map.base/ctl at core.c:42-50). Final claim counted as wrong; prose now states the check exists but cannot fire.

name: ab8500_regulator_set_mode
prose: Precondition: rdev is a regulator_dev whose driver data is NULL or an ab8500_regulator_info; mode is any unsigned int. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL (logged) if the driver data is NULL, before any lock is taken. Otherwise it takes shared_mode_mutex if info->shared_mode is non-NULL and releases it on every later return. mode other than REGULATOR_MODE_NORMAL or REGULATOR_MODE_IDLE returns -EINVAL with no register write and no change to update_val or lp_mode_req. For IDLE with a shared_mode, if shared_regulator->shared_mode->lp_mode_req is false it sets info->shared_mode->lp_mode_req to true and returns 0 without any register write or update_val change. Otherwise it selects the normal or idle value (from mode_val_* when mode_mask is non-zero, update_val_* otherwise) and, if mode_mask is non-zero or ab8500_regulator_is_enabled returns non-zero (which includes a negative error from that function), calls abx500_mask_and_set_register_interruptible; a negative result is returned immediately with update_val and lp_mode_req unchanged. After that, if mode_mask is zero it stores the value in info->update_val (even when no register write was made), and if shared_mode is non-NULL sets shared_mode->lp_mode_req to false for NORMAL and true for IDLE; it returns the register-write result (non-negative) or 0 if no write was made.
note: reviewer (round 15: the write also happens when is_enabled returns a negative error) right, ab8500.c:459 with is_enabled at 347-376. Function at ab8500.c:399-486; slice cut head.

name: _regulator_do_set_voltage
prose: Precondition: rdev, rdev->desc, rdev->desc->ops and rdev->constraints are valid; ops->list_voltage is required on the set_voltage_sel path. Postcondition: it reads the old voltage, emits the set_voltage trace and adds constraints->uV_offset to min_uV and max_uV. If the regulator is enabled and both set_voltage_time_sel and get_voltage_sel exist it reads the old selector and returns a negative result at once, without the set_voltage_complete trace, delay or notification. If ops->set_voltage exists it calls _regulator_call_set_voltage; for a non-negative result it computes best_val from list_voltage(selector) if that op exists or regulator_get_voltage_rdev otherwise, with no range check. Else if ops->set_voltage_sel exists it calls regulator_map_voltage; a negative result is kept as the return value; otherwise it sets best_val = list_voltage(mapped selector) and, if that value lies inside the offset-adjusted [min_uV, max_uV], either sets ret = 0 when the old selector equals the mapped selector or calls _regulator_set_voltage_sel_step (when vsel_step is set) or _regulator_call_set_voltage_sel, and if the value lies outside the range sets ret = -EINVAL. If neither op exists ret = -EINVAL. If ret is non-zero (negative or positive) it skips delay and notification, emits the set_voltage_complete trace with best_val, and returns ret as is. When ret is 0: if ops->set_voltage_time_sel exists the delay comes from it only when old_selector >= 0 and differs from the new selector (otherwise delay stays 0); if it does not exist, a delay is computed only when old_uV differs from best_val, using ops->set_voltage_time if present and _regulator_set_voltage_time otherwise. A negative delay is warned about and treated as 0; it then calls fsleep(delay), sends REGULATOR_EVENT_VOLTAGE_CHANGE with best_val only if best_val >= 0, emits the set_voltage_complete trace and returns 0. No lock or reference is taken or released by this function itself.
note: reviewer round 15 (delay fallback to set_voltage_time applies only when set_voltage_time_sel is absent) right, core.c:3767-3785; round 2 (complete trace not emitted on the early get_voltage_sel failure) is already how the prose reads, so wrong as a criticism of it; round 0 points (best_val<0 skips the notification; set_voltage path has no range check) right. Function at core.c:3703-3806.

name: da9062_map_buck_mode
prose: Precondition: none; mode may be any unsigned int. Postcondition: returns REGULATOR_MODE_STANDBY (0x8) when mode equals DA9063_BUCK_MODE_SLEEP (0x40), REGULATOR_MODE_FAST (0x1) when mode equals DA9063_BUCK_MODE_SYNC (0x80), REGULATOR_MODE_NORMAL (0x2) when mode equals DA9063_BUCK_MODE_AUTO (0xC0), and REGULATOR_MODE_INVALID (0) for every other value, including DA9063_BUCK_MODE_MANUAL (0x00). It reads and writes no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (mode == 0x40 && result == 8) || (mode == 0x80 && result == 1) || (mode == 0xC0 && result == 2) || (mode != 0x40 && mode != 0x80 && mode != 0xC0 && result == 0); */
note: da9062-regulator.c:101-113. The old prose took the DA9063_BUCK_MODE_* values as 0/1/2; registers.h:949-953 defines MANUAL=0x00, SLEEP=0x40, SYNC=0x80, AUTO=0xC0. Reviewer round 15 (STANDBY is 4, not 8) is wrong: consumer.h:82-86 has IDLE=0x4, STANDBY=0x8. Round 2 (SLEEP=0, SYNC=1, AUTO=2) also wrong.

name: ti_abb_init_table
prose: Precondition: dev has an of_node, abb points to an ABB instance (efuse_base and ldo_base may be NULL) and rinit_data points to the regulator init data. Postcondition: it counts the u32 elements of property "ti,abb_info" and returns that count's negative error if the property is missing; returns -EINVAL if the count is 0 or not a multiple of 6; returns -ENOMEM if the devm allocation of the info array or of the voltage table fails (abb->info is already set when the second allocation fails). It sets rdesc.n_voltages, rdesc.volt_table and current_info_idx = -EINVAL, then for each 6-tuple reads voltage, opp_sel, efuse_offset, rbb/fbb/vset masks (the return values of of_property_read_u32_index are ignored) and tracks min and max voltage. If efuse_base is NULL it only logs an error when any offset or mask is non-zero and goes to the opp_sel check; otherwise it reads the efuse word and sets opp_sel to TI_ABB_SLOW_OPP if the rbb mask matches, else TI_ABB_FAST_OPP if the fbb mask matches, else TI_ABB_NOMINAL_OPP if either mask is non-zero, else leaves the device-tree value. If ldo_base is NULL it logs an error when vset_mask is non-zero and moves to the next entry without checking opp_sel for that entry; otherwise vset = (efuse_val & vset_mask) >> __ffs(vset_mask) (vset_mask must be non-zero). For entries that reach the check, an opp_sel other than nominal, fast or slow returns -EINVAL (earlier assignments stay in place). After the loop it stores the minimum and maximum voltage into rinit_data->constraints.min_uV/max_uV and returns 0.
note: previously dropped as 'unnamed fragment'; real function ti_abb_init_table at ti-abb-regulator.c:497-621, slice cut the head. Fixed under the real name.

name: twl6030reg_get_status
prose: Precondition: rdev is a valid regulator device whose driver data points to a valid twlreg_info. Postcondition: it first reads the group register through twlreg_grp for every device type and returns that call's negative value if the read fails. It then reads VREG_STATE with twlreg_read; a failed read is not checked, so its negative errno is used as the state value. The state is val & TWL6030_CFG_STATE_MASK (0x3) when info->features has TWL6032_SUBCLASS, else TWL6030_CFG_STATE_APP(val), the application field bits 2-3. It returns REGULATOR_STATUS_NORMAL if the state is TWL6030_CFG_STATE_ON (1), REGULATOR_STATUS_STANDBY if it is TWL6030_CFG_STATE_SLEEP (3), and REGULATOR_STATUS_OFF for TWL6030_CFG_STATE_OFF, OFF2 or any other value, so a failed state read can yield any of the three results. It takes no lock and no reference.
note: reviewer (round 15: group read happens for both device types) right, twl6030-regulator.c:185-187. Function at 180-210.

name: qcom_pas_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device bound to this driver; its OF node may or may not carry "firmware-name" (and a second entry when the match data has dtb_firmware_name). Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if there is no match data, -EPROBE_DEFER if qcom_scm_is_available() is false, the error from reading "firmware-name" (or its second entry) when it is negative and not -EINVAL, and -ENOMEM if devm_rproc_alloc fails; none of these early returns has anything to undo. It then fills the qcom_pas structure and sets drvdata, and runs: device_init_wakeup(true), qcom_pas_alloc_memory_region, qcom_pas_assign_memory_region; a failure of any of these three jumps to a label that only calls device_init_wakeup(false) (so a failed assign is not followed by an unassign), qcom_pas_init_clock, qcom_pas_init_regulator and qcom_pas_pds_attach (failure of these goes through qcom_pas_unassign_memory_region and then the wakeup disable), qcom_q6v5_init (failure also detaches the proxy power domains), the glink, smd and pdm subdevice adds, qcom_add_sysmon_subdev (an error pointer here removes pdm, smd and glink subdevices and deinitialises q6v5 before the earlier steps), the ssr subdevice add and rproc_add (failure here also removes the ssr and sysmon subdevices first). It returns 0 if rproc_add succeeds, or the failing call's negative errno after the matching unwind steps. The rproc object comes from devm_rproc_alloc, so it is not freed explicitly in this function; drvdata is not cleared on failure.
note: reviewer (round 15: the rproc allocation is never freed on error) wrong: it is allocated with devm_rproc_alloc (qcom_q6v5_pas.c:711) so devres frees it; earlier prose overstated 'every completed step' undone (drvdata is left set), now qualified. Slice cut the head; function at 678-803.

name: ELF_GEN_FIELD_GET_SET(hdr, e_entry, u64)
prose: Macro-generated function elf_hdr_get_e_entry(class, arg), produced by ELF_GEN_FIELD_GET_SET(hdr, e_entry, u64). Precondition: arg points to a valid ELF header of the class given. Postcondition: if class == ELFCLASS32 it returns the e_entry of the struct elf32_hdr at arg cast to u64; for any other class value (not only ELFCLASS64) it returns the e_entry of struct elf64_hdr at arg cast to u64. It writes nothing.
note: remoteproc_elf_helpers.h:40-47 and 57.

name: ELF_GEN_FIELD_GET_SET(hdr, e_entry, u64)
prose: Macro-generated function elf_hdr_set_e_entry(class, arg, value), produced by ELF_GEN_FIELD_GET_SET(hdr, e_entry, u64). Precondition: arg points to a writable ELF header of the class given. Postcondition: it returns nothing; if class == ELFCLASS32 it stores value cast to the 32-bit field type into e_entry of the struct elf32_hdr at arg, so the high 32 bits of value are lost; for any other class value it stores value into e_entry of struct elf64_hdr.
note: remoteproc_elf_helpers.h:48-55 and 57.

name: ELF_STRUCT_SIZE(phdr)
prose: Macro-generated function elf_size_of_phdr(class), produced by ELF_STRUCT_SIZE(phdr). Postcondition: returns sizeof(struct elf32_phdr) if class == ELFCLASS32 and sizeof(struct elf64_phdr) for every other value of class. It reads and writes no state.
note: remoteproc_elf_helpers.h:87-94 and 97.

name: ELF_STRUCT_SIZE(shdr)
prose: Macro-generated function elf_size_of_shdr(class), produced by ELF_STRUCT_SIZE(shdr). Postcondition: returns sizeof(struct elf32_shdr) if class == ELFCLASS32 and sizeof(struct elf64_shdr) for every other value of class. It reads and writes no state.
note: remoteproc_elf_helpers.h:87-94 and 96.

name: omap_rtc_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device whose match data or platform_get_device_id() entry supplies the omap_rtc_device_type (the id entry is dereferenced without a NULL check) and which has a memory resource and two IRQs. Postcondition: returns -ENOMEM if the devm allocation fails, and the negative value of platform_get_irq for the timer or alarm IRQ, in both cases before any clock or runtime-PM change. It then tries the "ext-clk" clock, and the "int-clk" clock if that fails, and calls clk_prepare_enable on whichever it got, ignoring the result; if neither clock exists the probe continues with rtc->clk an error pointer. If the register mapping fails it calls clk_disable_unprepare (a no-op for an error pointer) and returns PTR_ERR of the mapping. Otherwise it sets drvdata, enables runtime PM and calls pm_runtime_get_sync (result ignored), unlocks the registers, configures interrupts, oscillator and control registers, locks the registers again, enables device wakeup and tries to allocate the RTC device, request one or two IRQs, register the pinctrl device and register the RTC. If any of those four steps fails it goes to a label that calls clk_disable_unprepare, device_init_wakeup(false), type->lock again, pm_runtime_put_sync and pm_runtime_disable and returns the error. After the RTC is registered it calls devm_rtc_nvmem_register (result ignored), installs omap_rtc_power_off as pm_power_off if this is a PMIC controller and pm_power_off is NULL, and returns 0.
note: reviewer round 15 mixed: right that clk_prepare_enable's result is ignored so success does not imply the clock is enabled (rtc-omap.c:761-762); wrong that clk_disable_unprepare on an ERR_PTR is a defect, since clk_disable and clk_unprepare return early for IS_ERR_OR_NULL (drivers/clk/clk.c:1093, 1231). Function at rtc-omap.c:727-910.

name: rtca3_set_time
prose: Precondition: dev has a rtca3_priv as driver data; tm points to a struct rtc_time. Postcondition: it holds the device spinlock (irqsave) from entry until return. It reads RCR2 and writes it with START cleared, then polls up to RTCA3_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_US for START to read clear; if that times out it returns the poll's error (-ETIMEDOUT) and no time register has been written (START was written clear but not confirmed). Otherwise it writes the BCD seconds, minutes, hours, weekday, day, month (tm_mon + 1) and year (tm_year % 100) registers, performs the dummy counter reads, writes RCR2 with the value originally read with START set (so the RTC is started even if it was stopped before), and returns the result of polling for START to read set: 0 if it does, -ETIMEDOUT if the poll times out after START was written.
note: rtc-renesas-rtca3.c:284-318. Only the polls are checked; the time writes are not read back.

name: rtca3_set_alarm
prose: Precondition: dev has a rtca3_priv as driver data; wkalrm points to a struct rtc_wkalrm. Postcondition: under the device spinlock it reads RCR2 and returns -EPERM at once if START is clear, with no register or alarm-step change. Otherwise it clears AIE in RCR1 and polls for it to read clear; on timeout it returns -ETIMEDOUT with nothing else changed (PIE untouched, step state untouched). It then writes the alarm registers (each with AR_ENB, year via tm_year % 100 and the year-alarm enable), does the dummy reads, sets the alarm step to RTCA3_ALRM_SSTEP_INIT, reinitialises the completion, sets PIE in RCR1 and polls for PIE to read set. If that poll times out, or if the later wait_for_completion_interruptible_timeout (500 ms) returns 0 or a negative value (timeout or interruption), it goes to a failure path that, under the lock, writes RCR1 with PIE cleared (and AIE still cleared), polls for PIE clear ignoring the result, sets the step state to RTCA3_ALRM_SSTEP_DONE and returns -ETIMEDOUT; the alarm registers stay programmed and AIE stays cleared in that case. If the wait succeeds, under the lock it calls rtca3_alarm_irq_set_helper to set or clear AIE according to wkalrm->enabled (it returns 0 or -ETIMEDOUT from its own poll), sets the step state to RTCA3_ALRM_SSTEP_DONE and returns that helper result. On the success path this function does not clear PIE itself; the periodic interrupt handler clears it after two periodic interrupts (rtc-renesas-rtca3.c:185-199).
note: rtc-renesas-rtca3.c:385-464. The earlier prose said PIE stays enabled in both cases; the handler disables it on completion, and the failure paths here disable it.
